title: fix(fields): read a `0` geolocation coordinate as a place, not as an absence (objectui#8055)
body:
Fixes #8055

`GeolocationField`'s **display/read** path carried two independent defects. Both are fixed
here; the card was right that fixing either alone leaves the other live, and the ablation
below proves the two apart by making each leg red on a *different* test.

## The class sweep — 23 conditional sites, not the card's 5

The card's "Affected sites" list is a snapshot of one measurement, so the file was swept
against the class criterion instead: **every "has a value" test whose operand may
legitimately be `0` must use nullish semantics, and no JSX conditional may carry a numeric
operand.** All 23 conditional/coercion sites in the file, with verdicts:

**Class hits — fixed (5).** The operand is a coordinate or an accuracy, all of which are
legitimately `0`, and three of them are JSX render expressions:

| site | before | why it is in the class |
|---|---|---|
| `formatLocation` | `if (!loc.latitude \|\| !loc.longitude) return ''` | falsy test on the parsed NUMBER |
| `openInMaps` | `if (!location.latitude \|\| !location.longitude) return` | same; refuses to open a valid place |
| readonly "View on map" | `{location.latitude && location.longitude && (…)}` | falsy test **and** numeric JSX operand |
| editable "View on map" | `{location.latitude && location.longitude && (…)}` | same shape |
| accuracy row | `{location.accuracy && (…)}` | same shape, on a value that is not exotic |

**Already correct — deliberately untouched (2).** `value={location.latitude ?? ''}` and its
longitude twin `value={location.longitude ?? ''}`. Both use `??`, both already showed `"0"`.
The card named the first; the second is its twin and is equally correct. Neither was "fixed"
into consistency with the broken guards — they are the live controls, see below.

**Not in the class (16), each for a stated reason.** `value || {}` (the operand is the
composite object, never legitimately `0`); `fieldValue ? Number(fieldValue) : null` (the
operand is the raw input **string**, and `'0'` is truthy — this is objectui#6848's pinned
emission site and stays as it is); `if (!navigator.geolocation)` (an API object); the map URL
template (an interpolation, not a test); `if (readonly)` and the `isLoading` ternary
(booleans); `{formatted ? … : …}` (a ternary on a **string**, whose `''` is the intended
sentinel — a ternary always renders exactly one branch, so no operand can leak);
`disabled={readonly || …}` ×3 and `className={… ? … : …}` ×2 (attribute values, not children,
and never numeric); `aria-invalid={!!error || !!…}` ×2 (explicitly coerced); and the two new
predicates themselves.

## The fix

One predicate that is **nullish and boolean-valued**, because the two defects need both
properties and neither implies the other:

- **nullish** so `0` counts as present — that is defect 1. A boolean-valued falsy guard would
  still call the equator "no location".
- **boolean** so `&&` can never hand React a number to render as a text node — that is
  defect 2. A nullish-but-numeric guard would still leak the `0`.

**The delta is exactly `0` and `-0`.** The predicate excludes `NaN`, as the old falsy guard
did. A bare `n != null` — the card's wording taken literally — would have started rendering
`"NaN, NaN"` at a surface that has always shown the placeholder for an unreadable coordinate:
a second display defect wearing the first one's fix. `Infinity`, `null`, `undefined`, a
missing half of the pair and a non-number all answer exactly as they did before. Pinned as a
control.

## Before / after

The new pins run against `main`'s version of the file reproduce the card's reading verbatim:

```
AssertionError: expected '—0' to contain '0.000000, 120.155100'
Expected: "0.000000, 120.155100"
Received: "—0"
```

Against `main`: **10 failed | 5 passed (15)**. The 5 that pass are *exactly* the 5 controls —
a control that goes red with the subject is not a control. After the fix: **15 passed (15)**.

## Ablation — two legs, expectations written before running

Each leg mutated the committed tree, proved the mutation was on disk (marker counts plus a
`git hash-object` comparison against the HEAD blob, with an empty hash treated as failure),
ran the pins, then restored and proved the restore by **state** — blob back to the HEAD value
and `git diff HEAD` empty — never by an exit code. Both legs restore under a
`trap … EXIT INT TERM` using `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH`. No build step is on the
path: the pins import the widget by a same-package relative **source** specifier, so `dist/`
never participates.

| leg | mutation | predicted | observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 — defect 1** | presence predicate body back to `!!n` (still boolean, so defect 2 stays fixed) | display returns to the empty placeholder; **no stray `0`** | **7 failed / 8 passed**, exactly as predicted |
| **2 — defect 2** | readonly guard back to `{location.latitude && location.longitude && (…)}` (presence still nullish) | coordinates still render; **the stray `0` returns** | **3 failed / 12 passed**, exactly as predicted |

**The legs are red on different tests, which is the point:**

- Red **only** under leg 1: the four "renders the coordinates / renders the accuracy row"
  tests. Under leg 2 they stay green, because `formatLocation` is still nullish.
- Red **only** under leg 2: `readonly: the coordinates row has no bare text-node children`,
  which failed with `expected [ '0' ] to deeply equal []` — the card's stray `0`, caught as
  the DOM shape it actually is. Under leg 1 it stays green, because a boolean guard renders
  nothing either way.
- Red under **both**: the two readonly "View on map" affordance tests. That is honest rather
  than sloppy — that single site carried both defects, so it is the user-facing consequence
  of either, and it is deliberately not the separator.

Defect 2's oracle is written as a DOM shape, not as a string diff: it reads the non-blank
text nodes that are **direct** children of the element holding the guard, which is exactly
where React puts a rendered numeric operand. It is deliberately not recursive — the accuracy
row legitimately renders `"Accuracy: ±"`, `"0"`, `"m"` as three nodes one level down.

Per the card's warning about assertions a `0` can fool: the positive half asserts
`toFixed(6)`'s own product (`"0.000000, 120.155100"`), which a stray `0` cannot satisfy;
`not.toContain(EM_DASH)` is never used alone.

## The two things the card did not measure

**Does the sibling `LocationField` carry the same shape? Measured: no — and ⛔ it was not
touched.** Its presence test is `isFiniteNumber` (`typeof n === 'number' &&
Number.isFinite(n)`), which admits `0`; its readonly render is
`{coordinateText(value) || EmptyValue}`, whose operand is a **string** (`"0, 0"` for a stored
zero, truthy), so no numeric operand exists to leak; its one other guard's operand is
`string | null`. It already answers this card's class criterion, by a documented ruling —
objectui#6272 option A1, whose docblock reasons about `0` explicitly — and a landed pin
already asserts the opposite of this defect: `LocationField.specShape.test.tsx`, *"carries a
zero coordinate as the real place it is, not as a default"*, asserting `textContent` is
`'0, 0'`. Re-run green. **No follow-up card is warranted.**

**Does any consumer depend on the current empty rendering? Measured: no.** No test, snapshot
or doc paragraph pins "a `0` geolocation coordinate displays as empty". Every zero-coordinate
fixture in the tree belongs to `LocationField`/`ObjectMap` and pins the opposite. The one
cross-package renderer of this widget is `plugin-detail`'s `InlineFieldInput`; its emptiness
authority tests use the non-zero `{ latitude: 30.2741, longitude: 120.1551 }` fixture and are
unaffected. Both suites re-run green (see below). **No pin was changed, and none needed to be.**

## Verification

| run | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/fields^...' run build` (dependency closure) | exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields run type-check` (`tsc --noEmit` **and** `tsconfig.test.json`, so the new pins are typechecked) | exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields run test` | **154 files, 2638 tests, all passed** |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail run test` (the consumer) | **155 files, 1415 tests, all passed** |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields run lint` | **0 errors** (987 pre-existing warnings; the changed files contribute none — the one warning on the widget is the pre-existing unused `field` param) |
| new pins, `packages/fields/src/__tests__/GeolocationZeroCoordinate-8055.test.tsx` | **15 passed** |

Measured at `3db5b0ee2`. Every heavy run went through the container's shared verify lock;
each is quoted from the wrapper's own `VERDICT command-exit` line, never a bare `$?`.

A first `type-check` returned **exit 2 — PREREQUISITE NOT MET** (workspace unbuilt,
`Cannot find module '@object-ui/components'`). That is NOT MEASURED, not red; it is recorded
here only so the green above is not mistaken for a re-run of nothing. It was re-run after the
closure build.

**Published surface: byte-identical.** `packages/fields/dist/index.d.ts` was built from
`origin/main`'s version of the widget and from this branch's and diffed: **identical**. The
two predicates and the narrowing type are module-private (no `export`), so `export *` in
`index.tsx` does not re-export them.

**Line-citation census (objectui#8875).** This change inserts ~59 lines near the top of
`GeolocationField.tsx`, moving every line below. `scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs`
reports **zero** citations naming that file, in either direction, and a five-syntax grep
confirms nothing in the tree addresses it by line. The two new files add no `path:line`
citation to the population. **No class-(A) repair was needed, and nothing class-(B) was
touched.** Re-checked against the final commit.

## 验收备注

- The `EmptyValue` placeholder path is unchanged and still correct for a genuinely absent
  coordinate, for a half pair (one coordinate present, one absent — a half pair must not
  invent the other half) and for `NaN`. All three are pinned as controls.
- `openInMaps` was fixed as part of the class sweep, not as a separate ask: it is the same
  falsy presence test one line from `formatLocation`, and it refused the same valid value a
  second time. Pinned by asserting the URL `window.open` receives.
- No out-of-scope findings were filed, and none are being withheld. The two open questions
  the card left were both measured and both came back negative (above); neither produces a
  follow-up card. Successor for the `LocationField` half: **none — nothing to carry.**
- ⛔ Not touched, deliberately: `LocationField`, the emission path (`handleFieldChange`, which
  objectui#6848 measured and pinned as already correct), and the two `?? ''` input bindings.
